thread:
Rae: Quick callout from the proofreading pass: we don't have a consistent policy on contractions in docs. Some pages use "don't" and others insist on "do not". Should we pick a default?
Omar: I vote for conversational tone: use contractions when it sounds natural (don't, can't), but keep formal phrasing in legal/compliance text.
Liliana: Agreed. Maybe a short rule: use contractions in user-facing guides and examples, avoid them in API reference and legal pages. We'll need a note in /docs/style.md.
Rae: Good. Also add a tiny exception for headings: keep headings concise and avoid contractions there ("Do not use X" vs "Don't use X").
Sam: I'll update the style guide blurb: one paragraph + a couple of examples. Want to include a regex check?
Omar: Regex is tricky but a warning in the PR template could work: checkbox "Checked tone and contractions per style guide." Plus rely on reviewers.
DocsBot: reminder: docs linter can flag sentence-case vs title-case headings but not contractions currently. Feature request logged: DOCS-512.
Liliana: Can someone draft the exact wording? Short, prescriptive. I'll review and merge.
Rae: Draft suggestion: "Use contractions in conversational docs and tutorials (e.g., don't, we're). Avoid contractions in API reference, migration guides, and legal text. Keep headings contraction-free"
Sam: Nice — I'll open a small PR to /docs/style.md with that text and examples by EOD.
Omar: I'll add the PR template checkbox and link to the style section.
Liliana: Once merged, I'll run a quick grep to find obvious mismatches and open follow-up PRs for any large pages.
DocsBot: queued job: docs-tone-check (post-merge scan).
